paragraphs.text: In those days, when there was again a great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them,
paragraphs.original: Ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις πάλιν πολλοῦ ὄχλου ὄντος καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων τί φάγωσιν, προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς λέγει αὐτοῖς·
paragraphs.translit: En ekeinais tais hēmerais palin pollou ochlou ontos kai mē echontōn ti phagōsin, proskalesamenos tous mathētas legei autois·

paragraphs.text: I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat:
paragraphs.original: Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν·
paragraphs.translit: Splanchnizomai epi ton ochlon hoti ēdē hēmerai treis prosmenousin moi kai ouk echousin ti phagōsin·

paragraphs.text: and if I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way; and some of them are come from far.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἀπολύσω αὐτοὺς νήστεις εἰς οἶκον αὐτῶν, ἐκλυθήσονται ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ· καί τινες αὐτῶν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἥκασιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean apolysō autous nēsteis eis oikon autōn, eklythēsontai en tē hodō· kai tines autōn apo makrothen hēkasin.

paragraphs.text: And his disciples answered him, Whence shall one be able to fill these men with bread here in a desert place?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι Πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπʼ ἐρημίας;
paragraphs.translit: kai apekrithēsan autō hoi mathētai autou hoti Pothen toutous dynēsetai tis hōde chortasai artōn epʼ erēmias;

paragraphs.text: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτούς· Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά.
paragraphs.translit: kai ērōta autous· Posous echete artous; hoi de eipan· Hepta.

paragraphs.text: And he commandeth the multitude to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and having given thanks, he brake, and gave to his disciples, to set before them; and they set them before the multitude.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παραγγέλλει τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν καὶ παρέθηκαν τῷ ὄχλῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai parangellei tō ochlō anapesein epi tēs gēs· kai labōn tous hepta artous eucharistēsas eklasen kai edidou tois mathētais autou hina paratithōsin kai parethēkan tō ochlō.

paragraphs.text: And they had a few small fishes: and having blessed them, he commanded to set these also before them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶχον ἰχθύδια ὀλίγα· καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτὰ εἶπεν καὶ ταῦτα παρατιθέναι.
paragraphs.translit: kai eichon ichthydia oliga· kai eulogēsas auta eipen kai tauta paratithenai.

paragraphs.text: And they ate, and were filled: and they took up, of broken pieces that remained over, seven baskets.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔφαγον καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν περισσεύματα κλασμάτων ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας.
paragraphs.translit: kai ephagon kai echortasthēsan, kai ēran perisseumata klasmatōn hepta spyridas.

paragraphs.text: And they were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δὲ ὡς τετρακισχίλιοι. καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de hōs tetrakischilioi. kai apelysen autous.

paragraphs.text: And straightway he entered into the boat with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐμβὰς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά.
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys embas eis to ploion meta tōn mathētōn autou ēlthen eis ta merē Dalmanoutha.

paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, trying him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν αὐτῷ, ζητοῦντες παρʼ αὐτοῦ σημεῖον ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai exēlthon hoi Pharisaioi kai ērxanto syzētein autō, zētountes parʼ autou sēmeion apo tou ouranou, peirazontes auton.

paragraphs.text: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναστενάξας τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ζητεῖ σημεῖον; ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, εἰ δοθήσεται τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ σημεῖον.
paragraphs.translit: kai anastenaxas tō pneumati autou legei· Ti hē genea hautē zētei sēmeion; amēn legō hymin, ei dothēsetai tē genea tautē sēmeion.

paragraphs.text: And he left them, and again entering into [the boat] departed to the other side.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς πάλιν ἐμβὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apheis autous palin embas apēlthen eis to peran.

paragraphs.text: And they forgot to take bread; and they had not in the boat with them more than one loaf.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐπελάθοντο λαβεῖν ἄρτους, καὶ εἰ μὴ ἕνα ἄρτον οὐκ εἶχον μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai epelathonto labein artous, kai ei mē hena arton ouk eichon methʼ heautōn en tō ploiō.

paragraphs.text: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διεστέλλετο αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε, βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῆς ζύμης Ἡρῴδου.
paragraphs.translit: kai diestelleto autois legōn· Horate, blepete apo tēs zymēs tōn Pharisaiōn kai tēs zymēs Hērōdou.

paragraphs.text: And they reasoned one with another, saying, We have no bread.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἀλλήλους ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai dielogizonto pros allēlous hoti artous ouk echousin.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus perceiving it saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? do ye not yet perceive, neither understand? have ye your heart hardened?
paragraphs.original: καὶ γνοὺς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε; οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ συνίετε; πεπωρωμένην ἔχετε τὴν καρδίαν ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: kai gnous legei autois· Ti dialogizesthe hoti artous ouk echete; oupō noeite oude syniete; pepōrōmenēn echete tēn kardian hymōn;

paragraphs.text: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
paragraphs.original: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες οὐ βλέπετε καὶ ὦτα ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούετε; καὶ οὐ μνημονεύετε
paragraphs.translit: ophthalmous echontes ou blepete kai ōta echontes ouk akouete; kai ou mnēmoneuete

paragraphs.text: When I brake the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους ἔκλασα εἰς τοὺς πεντακισχιλίους, πόσους κοφίνους κλασμάτων πλήρεις ἤρατε; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δώδεκα.
paragraphs.translit: hote tous pente artous eklasa eis tous pentakischilious, posous kophinous klasmatōn plēreis ērate; legousin autō· Dōdeka.

paragraphs.text: And when the seven among the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces took ye up? And they say unto him, Seven.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ εἰς τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους, πόσων σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων ἤρατε; καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἑπτά.
paragraphs.translit: hote kai tous hepta eis tous tetrakischilious, posōn spyridōn plērōmata klasmatōn ērate; kai legousin autō· Hepta.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Do ye not yet understand?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Οὔπω συνίετε;
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois· Oupō syniete;

paragraphs.text: And they come unto Bethsaida. And they bring to him a blind man, and beseech him to touch him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Βηθσαϊδάν. καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ τυφλὸν καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψηται.
paragraphs.translit: Kai erchontai eis Bēthsaidan. kai pherousin autō typhlon kai parakalousin auton hina autou hapsētai.

paragraphs.text: And he took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village; and when he had spit on his eyes, and laid his hands upon him, he asked him, Seest thou aught?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ἐξήνεγκεν αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς κώμης, καὶ πτύσας εἰς τὰ ὄμματα αὐτοῦ, ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ, ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Εἴ τι βλέπεις;
paragraphs.translit: kai epilabomenos tēs cheiros tou typhlou exēnenken auton exō tēs kōmēs, kai ptysas eis ta ommata autou, epitheis tas cheiras autō, epērōta auton· Ei ti blepeis;

paragraphs.text: And he looked up, and said, I see men; for I behold [them] as trees, walking.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναβλέψας ἔλεγεν· Βλέπω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὅτι ὡς δένδρα ὁρῶ περιπατοῦντας.
paragraphs.translit: kai anablepsas elegen· Blepō tous anthrōpous hoti hōs dendra horō peripatountas.

paragraphs.text: Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes; and he looked stedfastly, and was restored, and saw all things clearly.
paragraphs.original: εἶτα πάλιν ἐπέθηκεν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ διέβλεψεν καὶ ἀπεκατέστη καὶ ἐνέβλεπεν τηλαυγῶς ἅπαντα.
paragraphs.translit: eita palin epethēken tas cheiras epi tous ophthalmous autou, kai dieblepsen kai apekatestē kai eneblepen tēlaugōs hapanta.

paragraphs.text: And he sent him away to his home, saying, Do not even enter into the village.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ λέγων· Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην εἰσέλθῃς.
paragraphs.translit: kai apesteilen auton eis oikon autou legōn· Mēde eis tēn kōmēn eiselthēs.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus went forth, and his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi: and on the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Who do men say that I am?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς κώμας Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου· καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐπηρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων αὐτοῖς· Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι;
paragraphs.translit: Kai exēlthen ho Iēsous kai hoi mathētai autou eis tas kōmas Kaisareias tēs Philippou· kai en tē hodō epērōta tous mathētas autou legōn autois· Tina me legousin hoi anthrōpoi einai;

paragraphs.text: And they told him, saying, John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but others, One of the prophets.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, καὶ ἄλλοι Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ὅτι εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan autō legontes hoti Iōannēn ton baptistēn, kai alloi Ēlian, alloi de hoti heis tōn prophētōn.

paragraphs.text: And he asked them, But who say ye that I am? Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
paragraphs.original: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι; ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός.
paragraphs.translit: kai autos epērōta autous· Hymeis de tina me legete einai; apokritheis ho Petros legei autō· Sy ei ho christos.

paragraphs.text: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai epetimēsen autois hina mēdeni legōsin peri autou.

paragraphs.text: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστῆναι·
paragraphs.translit: Kai ērxato didaskein autous hoti dei ton hyion tou anthrōpou polla pathein kai apodokimasthēnai hypo tōn presbyterōn kai tōn archiereōn kai tōn grammateōn kai apoktanthēnai kai meta treis hēmeras anastēnai·

paragraphs.text: And he spake the saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρρησίᾳ τὸν λόγον ἐλάλει. καὶ προσλαβόμενος ὁ Πέτρος αὐτὸν ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai parrēsia ton logon elalei. kai proslabomenos ho Petros auton ērxato epitiman autō.

paragraphs.text: But he turning about, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and saith, Get thee behind me, Satan; for thou mindest not the things of God, but the things of men.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἐπιστραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐπετίμησεν Πέτρῳ καὶ λέγει· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: ho de epistrapheis kai idōn tous mathētas autou epetimēsen Petrō kai legei· Hypage opisō mou, Satana, hoti ou phroneis ta tou theou alla ta tōn anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: And he called unto him the multitude with his disciples, and said unto them, If any man would come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai proskalesamenos ton ochlon syn tois mathētais autou eipen autois· Ei tis thelei opisō mou elthein, aparnēsasthō heauton kai aratō ton stauron autou kai akoloutheitō moi.

paragraphs.text: For whosoever would save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel`s shall save it.
paragraphs.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ἀπολέσει τὴν ⸄ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ⸅ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου σώσει αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: hos gar ean thelē tēn psychēn autou sōsai apolesei autēn· hos dʼ an apolesei tēn ⸄psychēn autou⸅ heneken emou kai tou euangeliou sōsei autēn.

paragraphs.text: For what doth it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?
paragraphs.original: τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἄνθρωπον κερδῆσαι τὸν κόσμον ὅλον καὶ ζημιωθῆναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ti gar ōphelei anthrōpon kerdēsai ton kosmon holon kai zēmiōthēnai tēn psychēn autou;

paragraphs.text: For what should a man give in exchange for his life?
paragraphs.original: τί γὰρ δοῖ ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: ti gar doi anthrōpos antallagma tēs psychēs autou;

paragraphs.text: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of man also shall be ashamed of him, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
paragraphs.original: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ μοιχαλίδι καὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται αὐτὸν ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων.
paragraphs.translit: hos gar ean epaischynthē me kai tous emous logous en tē genea tautē tē moichalidi kai hamartōlō, kai ho hyios tou anthrōpou epaischynthēsetai auton hotan elthē en tē doxē tou patros autou meta tōn angelōn tōn hagiōn.
